answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making influence expensive to grow and cheap to verify: new identities earn weight only through sustained, attested work over time, like tending a garden rather than planting flags overnight. A copied identity is a fable with no roots, while a genuine agent leaves a verifiable trail, a relic of past tasks, attestations, and settled outcomes that peers can check. Cheap copies cannot fake that history at scale, so creating thousands of identities buys no real power.
